episodes.195312: A fairly weak shortwave slipped by the forecast region to the north, but provided sufficient  synoptic support to yield scattered high-based convective development, and some convection resulted in severe wind gusts.
episodes.195612: More heavy rain occurred due to plenty of moisture and lift around the Blue Ridge Mountains of central Virginia. The ground was already saturated due to previous rainfall, so this led to more instances of flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.195650: A shortwave trough moved through eastern Utah and western Colorado, generating some isolated storms that produced strong gusty outflow winds as low levels remained dry. One particular storm produced a severe wind gust in Grand County.
episodes.195925: A very strong thunderstorm over Fallon County produced a severe wind gust at the Baker Airport. In addition, a synoptically-driven wind resulted in a few high wind gusts southeast of Red Lodge, Montana, as well as near the Busby, Montana area.
episodes.196864: Scattered thunderstorms just north of a frontal boundary produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of central Virginia.
episodes.197031: Multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms associated with the remnant moisture of Tropical Storm Helene passed across the region, producing localized heavy rainfall across soils that were already moist from previous rainfall. Rainfall rates in several of the storms that developed ranged from between three and five inches per hour and, in a few cases, were higher. Creeks that were already high from recent rainfall did not need much additional runoff to be forced out of their banks and flood nearby roads.
episodes.197269: Southwest steering flow and high moisture produced scattered afternoon showers and storms that approached the FL east coast in the afternoon where convergence spawned a thunderstorm that produced a brief gustnado in the Grand Haven area.

Flooding was reported at the intersection Old Lynchburg Road and Dudley Mountain Road.

The intersection of of Craigtown Road and Naked Mountain Road was washed out due to flowing water.
Mill Pond Road was closed due to high flowing water from Cove Creek being out of its banks.
The roadway near the intersection of Rockfish River Road and Laurel Road was flooded.
The Baker Airport reported a wind gust of 67 mph.
Jericho Road was closed due to flooding near Christians Creek and Route 250.

The Mechums River near White Hall rose above flood stage. Water approached homes along Free Union Road. ||The water level crested at 22.93 feet at 7:45 AM EST on the 30th.

The South River near Dooms, VA reached minor flood stage of 11 feet. The water level crested at 11.63 feet at 4:30 AM EST on the 30th. Agricultural flooding occurred near the river. Flooding also occurred in the city of Waynesboro to the south.
Standing water was reported at the intersection of Flinn Lane and West Creek Road.
Rockfish River Road was closed due to flowing water.
Starvale Lane was closed due to high water over the road.
The water level rose above the flood stage of 9.5 feet along the South River at Harrison, cresting at 10.31 feet at 10:30 AM EST on the 30th. The end of Route 770 was flooded.
The Middle River near Grottoes rose above the flood stage of 12 feet, cresting at 14.57 feet at 5:15 PM EST on the 30th. Fields along the river were flooded.

The river gauge located on the South Fork of Shenandoah River near Lynnwood reached minor flood stage (16 feet) with crest of 16.7 feet. At 16 feet, lowlands near the river, and low spots of Power Dam Road, begin to flood.

Runoff from heavy rainfall over nearly saturated soil caused a portion of Roanoke Street to be flooded and impassible for a brief period of time. Rainfall rates at times were close to four inches per hour, with rainfall totals of around 1.5 inches falling in a 90 minute period. Crest Unit Streamflow peaked at 464 cfs/mi^2 at around 4:30 pm EDT.

A thunderstorm produced around 1.5 inches of rain falling at rates exceeding four inches per hour. This rain fell across ground that was nearly saturated from rainfall during Tropical Storm Helene a few days earlier.  At 6 pm EDT, FLASH CREST Unit Streamflow was as high as 400 cfs/mi^2, while the 1-hour QPE was 135 percent of FFG values.  This rainfall flooded Broad Hollow Road, making it impassible until the flooding receded. No damage was reported to the road.

A slow moving thunderstorm produced about four inches of rain within a 75-minute period, with rates approaching five inches per hour.  At 7 pm EDT, CREST Unit Flow peaked at an exceptional 2,612 cfs/mi^2, while rainfall amounts rose to 220 percent of Flash Flood Guidance. Runoff from this rainfall caused several roads in the Ajax area through Gretna area of Pittsylvania County to become flooded and impassible until the water receded, including Jasmine Road (Highway 778), Sandy Road, Grassland Drive and West Gretna Road. Millstream Drive was reported washed out by Georges Creek, making the road impassible until repairs can be completed. Whitehorn Creek reportedly overflowed its bank across Chalk Level Road, making the road impassible until the flooding receded. At least four other roads, names unknown, were flooded and impassible along the western and northwestern sides of Gretna.

Slow moving thunderstorms produced between 2 and 2.5 inches of rainfall across central Campbell County during the evening of September 30th, with rain at times falling at a rate of four inches per hour.  The CREST Unit Flow peaked at 270 cfs/mi^2, while rainfall estimates were 70 to 80 percent of Flash Flood Guidance. Regardless, the short but intense rainfall was enough to produce runoff that flooded multiple roads, making them impassible for short periods of time: Depot Street, Crows Road, Brookneal Highway near Gladys, and Campbell Highway in Rustburg. Flooding also occurred along Village Highway, where one vehicle was washed off the road, as well as along Rocky Road. It is uncertain if there was any damage to the vehicle. No damage to the roads were reported.

A thunderstorm produced around 1.5 inches of rain falling at rates of around three inches per hour. This rain fell across ground that was very moist from rainfall occurring during Tropical Storm Helene a few days earlier. Runoff from the rainfall caused multiple roads located northwest of the town of Appomattox to become flooded and impassible with several inches of flowing water across them. This included Phelps Branch Road where it intersects Phelps Branch, as well as North Creek Road at North Creek. No damage to the roads were reported, which were open to traffic after the water receded.
